Here in Dodoma the rain does not come the way it used to. Last year we waited long for the rain, and my neighbor who bought fertilizer saw his money burn in the sun because the maize did not grow well. I do what my father did — I put the manure from my goats and the kraal on the plot before planting, and I keep the seed from last year's harvest because it knows this soil. I cannot spend shillings on fertilizer and improved seed when the sky may close on me. My wife and I will work this plot ourselves, and when it is time to weed I may call one or two young men from the village for a few days if the grass is too much.
